Area charts emphasize the magnitude of one or more quantities over an ordered axis by filling the region under the line; stacked variants decompose a total into layers, and a streamgraph stacks layers around a wobbling baseline for a smooth composition-over-time view. In biomedical research they fit immune-population dynamics and cohort accrual. `CairoMakie` composes them from `band!` layers.

## Example

![](../images/Julia/AreaPlot_demo.png){fig-align="center" width="80%"}

## Setup

- System Requirements: Cross-platform (Linux/MacOS/Windows)
- Programming Language: **Julia**
- Dependencies: `CairoMakie`, `DataFrames`, `Statistics`

```{julia}
#| label: packages-setup
#| output: false
using CairoMakie
using DataFrames
using Statistics
using Random
```

## Data Preparation

We simulate weekly flow-cytometry counts of three lymphocyte populations across an 8-week vaccination study.

```{julia}
#| label: data-prep
Random.seed!(71)

weeks = collect(1.0:8)
n_weeks = length(weeks)
counts = DataFrame(
    Week = weeks,
    CD4 = 400 .* exp.(0.10 .* weeks) .+ 25 .* randn(n_weeks),
    CD8 = 300 .* exp.(0.16 .* weeks) .+ 22 .* randn(n_weeks),
    B = 200 .* exp.(0.06 .* weeks) .+ 15 .* randn(n_weeks))
series = [counts.CD4, counts.CD8, counts.B]
series_names = ["CD4 T", "CD8 T", "B cells"]
band_colors = [:steelblue, :plum, :seagreen]
```

## Visualization

### Single Area Chart

`band!` fills the region between a lower and an upper bound — the minimal emphasis form for one series.

```{julia}
#| label: fig-jl-area-single
#| fig-cap: "CD8 T-cell counts over the vaccination course"
#| width: 480
fig = Figure(size = (460, 340))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1], xlabel = "Week", ylabel = "Cell count (×10\$^3\$)")
band!(ax, counts.Week, zero(weeks), counts.CD8; color = (:plum, 0.45))
lines!(ax, counts.Week, counts.CD8; color = :magenta3, linewidth = 1.8)
hidespines!(ax, :t, :r)
fig
```

### Stacked Area Chart

Cumulative sums define each layer's bounds; drawing the bands bottom-up with white strokes keeps the layers separable.

```{julia}
#| label: fig-jl-area-stacked
#| fig-cap: "Stacked lymphocyte counts across the study weeks"
#| width: 520
upper = reduce(hcat, series) |> x -> cumsum(x, dims = 2)   # n_weeks × 3
lower = hcat(zeros(n_weeks), upper[:, 1:end-1])

fig = Figure(size = (500, 360))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1], xlabel = "Week", ylabel = "Cell count (×10\$^3\$)")
for k in 1:3
    band!(ax, counts.Week, lower[:, k], upper[:, k];
          color = (band_colors[k], 0.85), strokecolor = :white, strokewidth = 0.6)
end
hidespines!(ax, :t, :r)
elements = [PolyElement(polycolor = band_colors[k]) for k in 1:3]
Legend(fig[1, 2], elements, series_names, framevisible = false)
fig
```

### Streamgraph

A streamgraph offsets the whole stack around a symmetric ("wiggle"-style) baseline so the eye follows each band's shape rather than a zero line.

```{julia}
#| label: fig-jl-area-stream
#| fig-cap: "Streamgraph of lymphocyte composition (symmetric baseline)"
#| width: 560
total = vec(sum(reduce(hcat, series), dims = 2))
baseline = .-total ./ 2            # symmetric baseline centers the stack

fig = Figure(size = (560, 360))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1], xlabel = "Week",
          ylabel = "Cell count (×10\$^3\$, offset baseline)")
for k in 1:3
    band!(ax, counts.Week, baseline .+ (k == 1 ? 0.0 : sum(series[1:k-1]; dims = 1)[1]),
          baseline .+ sum(series[1:k]; dims = 1)[1];
          color = (band_colors[k], 0.9), strokecolor = :white, strokewidth = 0.6)
end
hidespines!(ax, :t, :r, :l)
hideydecorations!(ax)
elements = [PolyElement(polycolor = band_colors[k]) for k in 1:3]
Legend(fig[1, 2], elements, series_names, framevisible = false)
fig
```
